title: Compact generators and finite-Tor constructible compactness on finite-type etale sites without separatedness
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. No separatedness of $T$ over $k$ is assumed. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and standard cohomology [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Call $E$ bounded constructible if $H^i(E)=0$ for all but finitely many $i$ and each $H^i(E)$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Say $E$ has finite Tor amplitude if there are integers $r\le s$ such that for every sheaf $N$ of $C$-modules placed in degree zero, $H^i(E\otimes_C^L N)=0$ for every $i\notin[r,s]$.

Every bounded constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude is compact [def-pc-compact-object] in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$. There exist a set $S$ in the indexing universe and a family $(E_s)_{s\in S}$ of bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude such that, for every morphism $h:A\to B$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, if postcomposition $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],B)$ is bijective for all $s\in S$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $h$ is an isomorphism. The category has arbitrary set-indexed coproducts and is locally small in the corresponding Hom universe.

source.place: Section 6.4, hypothesis preceding Example 6.4.1; Example 6.4.1; Lemmas 6.4.2 and 6.4.5; Proposition 6.4.8 (printed pp. 48–49). Bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes agree with the perfect-value constructible complexes of Definition 6.3.1 by Lemma 6.3.7 (printed pp. 45–46) and the finite-Tor perfectness criterion. The section assumes qcqs, not separatedness; finite-type schemes here are Noetherian and qcqs.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. No diagonal of $T/k$ is used. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ is Grothendieck abelian. Use the convention [def-weil-size-convention] that the sites are small in the chosen larger indexing universe. On that small site, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] supplies K-injective resolutions, and [lem-pc-derived-category-locally-small] gives local smallness in the Hom universe of $\mathcal A$. By [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], arbitrary set-indexed coproducts in $D(\mathcal A)$ are represented by termwise sums. This includes the empty coproduct.

source.place: Section 6.4, qcqs ambient hypothesis; standard derived-category prerequisites supplied by the cited Grothendieck and K-injective statements.

proof.text: For every locally closed stratum $V$ of $T$, let $j:V\hookrightarrow\overline V$ be its open immersion into the closure and $g:\overline V\hookrightarrow T$ the closed immersion. If $L$ is finite locally constant on $V$ with flat stalks, [lem-pur-etale-lisse-stratum-compact] says exactly that $g_*j_!L$ is compact in the full unbounded ordinary etale derived category. The closed direct image is exact by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement]; hence its right derived image agrees with the termwise image by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], and the generators $Rg_*j_!L$ occurring in the Noetherian complement of [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] are these very objects. The lemma on strata applies because $T$ is finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$ and the given coefficient ring is finite and $\ell$-primary.

source.place: Lemma 6.4.6 and proof of Proposition 6.4.8, last paragraph, applied to the lisse flat generators of the cited Noetherian devissage.

proof.text: Compact objects form a thick subcategory here. For shifts, use $\operatorname{Hom}(P[n],K)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,K[-n])$; shifts preserve coproducts because they are equivalences. Closure under cones is [lem-sc-compact-cone], with precisely the coproduct universe fixed in step 1. For a retract $P\xrightarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}P$ with $ba=1$, the coproduct comparison for $P$ is a retract of that for $Q$, so its inverse is obtained by composing the inclusion, the inverse comparison for $Q$, and the retraction. The zero object is compact, and compactness is invariant under isomorphism. Apply the Noetherian complement of [sk-lem-sf-flat-model], which explicitly applies on the ordinary etale site for every Noetherian scheme and finite commutative coefficient ring: every bounded constructible finite-Tor complex lies in the thick subcategory generated by the $Rg_*j_!L$ of step 2. It is therefore compact. In this application finite Tor amplitude means that some integers $r\le s$ satisfy $H^i(K\otimes_C^L N[0])=0$ for every sheaf $N$ of $C$-modules and every $i\notin[r,s]$; this is precisely the Tor condition specified in the Noetherian complement.

source.place: Proposition 6.4.8, reverse inclusion, using the existing Noetherian finite-Tor flat-model devissage instead of restating a general compactness theorem.

proof.text: Choose a set $S$ of representatives $u_s:U_s\to T$ of the affine objects of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover]; these objects cover every object of the site. Work in the fixed indexing universe containing this small presentation. Put $E_s=u_{s!}C_{U_s}[0]$. Since $T$ and $U_s$ are qcqs, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible] with $M=C$ makes $E_s$ a constructible sheaf. It is flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat], applied to the constant ring sheaf; the identification with that free extension is part of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible]. A flat sheaf in degree zero has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: tensoring an acyclic complex with it remains acyclic, since its exact tensor functor preserves kernels and images. It is consequently K-flat, so its derived tensor with any degree-zero sheaf is the ordinary degree-zero tensor by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Thus each $E_s$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Apply step 3 to this bounded constructible finite-Tor object to conclude that $E_s$ is compact.

source.place: Lemma 6.4.5(1) and the coherent generators in the first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 6.4.8; constructibility and flatness supplied by the cited site lemmas.

proof.text: For any module sheaf $F$, the sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and the explicit free Yoneda bijection [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] give a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(u_{s!}C_{U_s},F)\cong F(U_s)$. The identification with the sheafification of the free ring-presheaf module is the $M=C$ clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible]. If $I$ is a K-injective complex representing $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies derived morphisms into $QI$ with homotopy classes of chain maps. A chain map from $E_s[n]$ to $I$ is a section of $I^{-n}(U_s)$ killed by the differential; two such maps are homotopic exactly when their sections differ by a boundary in $I^{-n}(U_s)$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(E_s[n],K)\cong H^{-n}(I(U_s))$. All identifications are natural in maps of target complexes, because the free Yoneda bijection is natural and both chain-map and homotopy formulas use composition.

source.place: Proposition 6.4.8, first paragraph: expand detection by free etale generators, using K-injectives rather than an unmentioned resolution theorem.

proof.text: Let $h:A\to B$ satisfy the Hom-bijection hypothesis of the item. Choose K-injective representatives $I_A,I_B$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the morphism $h$ is represented, under these isomorphisms, by a chain map $f:I_A\to I_B$. Step 5 shows that $H^q(I_A(U_s))\to H^q(I_B(U_s))$ is bijective for every $s$ and $q$ (put $n=-q$). These sectionwise bijections imply that $H^q(f)$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. Indeed a local section of a cohomology sheaf is locally represented by a cocycle; refine to an affine basis object $U_s$. Surjectivity on $H^q(I(U_s))$ lifts a target cocycle modulo a boundary to a source cocycle, proving local surjectivity on cohomology sheaves. For injectivity, represent a source class locally by a cocycle and, if its image vanishes as a sheaf class, shrink until its image is a boundary; refine once more to an affine basis object. Injectivity on $H^q(I(U_s))$ then makes the source cocycle a boundary there. Thus the kernel sheaf is zero as well. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $Qf$, and hence $h$, is invertible. This proves the required morphism-detection assertion for the set $S$ and family just constructed.

source.place: Proposition 6.4.8, compact generation: explicit local cocycle and boundary proof of detection on the small affine etale basis.

split_report.summary: Preserved every hypothesis and conclusion, including nonseparated T, arbitrary algebraically closed k and unbounded targets. Split finite-Tor compactness through the existing Noetherian finite-ring flat-model devissage and a smaller lisse-stratum compactness input; constructed a small affine-etale family and proved its morphism detection via natural K-injective section-Hom formulas and local cocycle/boundary arguments. Added one statement-only Bhatt–Scholze input; searched project Lean, whole DAG, current blueprint and Mathlib, twice by concept. No SGA route, Lean edits or builds. Retry audit: made the small-site universe convention explicit and removed the redundant free-extension compactness node, since step 3 already proves compactness of the finite-Tor free generators constructed in step 4.
split_report.blueprint: Adic-stage paragraph: "For Λ in {O_E,E,Qlb}, use respectively derived inverse limits, rationalization, and the common-stage construction ... of the compatible finite-level functors"; finite-level compact generators used to control coproducts of coefficient-system adjoints. Steps 1–3 give finite-Tor compactness; steps 4–6 give the compact generator family, size and detection needed by the finite-stage right-adjoint coproduct argument.

General ordinary etale module-category theorem supplies the Grothendieck category for coproducts and resolutions.
General small ringed-site resolution theorem supplies representatives of arbitrary unbounded objects.
General categorical size theorem controls the Hom universe of the ordinary derived category.
General Grothendieck derived-category coproduct theorem gives arbitrary set-indexed sums.
Only exactness of ordinary etale closed direct image is used; it identifies the stratum generators.
General exact-functor theorem identifies Rg_* with g_* on bounded stratum sheaves.
The explicitly stated Noetherian finite-ring ordinary-etale complement supplies thick generation, a generic devissage tool for the compactness argument.
General compact-object closure under cones, in the same coproduct universe.
General small-site basis theorem supplies a set of affine etale objects and cover-density.
General qcqs constructibility theorem and free-sheaf identification for the chosen generators.
General ringed-site flatness theorem verifies finite Tor amplitude of the free generators.
General module-valued Yoneda bijection, not just full faithfulness, identifies Hom with sections.
General unbounded K-injective full-faithfulness theorem computes all shifted Hom tests and represents h by a chain map.

lean.statement: theorem finiteRing_compactGenerators {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓprime : Nat.Prime ℓ) (hℓunit : IsUnit (ℓ : k)) {T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] {C : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing C] [Finite C] (hC : ∃ n : ℕ, (ℓ : C) ^ n = 0) : ∃ (hcoprod : HasCoproducts.{u + 1} (DerivedCategoryModule C T)), LocallySmall.{u + 1} (DerivedCategoryModule C T) ∧ (∀ E : DerivedCategoryModule C T, DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible C T E ∧ (∃ r s : ℤ, r ≤ s ∧ DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn C T r s E) → @IsCompactObject (DerivedCategoryModule C T) _ _ hcoprod E) ∧ (∃ (S : Type (u + 1)) (E : S → DerivedCategoryModule C T), (∀ s : S, DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible C T (E s) ∧ ∃ r t : ℤ, r ≤ t ∧ DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn C T r t (E s)) ∧ ∀ (A B : DerivedCategoryModule C T) (h : A ⟶ B), (∀ (s : S) (n : ℤ), Function.Bijective (fun (φ : (E s)⟦n⟧ ⟶ A) ↦ φ ≫ h)) → IsIso h)
